Chapter 13: The Road Ahead—Choosing a Legacy
As the story of the sixth extinction keeps unfolding, there’s this question that just hangs in the air—what kind of legacy are we really leaving behind? Imagine, years from now, what will future generations inherit? What stories will they tell when they look back at the choices we’re making right now?
Picture this for a moment: a grandparent strolling through a city park, hand in hand with a child. She points out the birds and the trees that still dot the landscape. But there’s a question in her eyes—what will this place look like when her grandchild grows up? It’s those choices we make—about energy, about food, about how we use land and water—that will shape the world for centuries to come.
And here’s something worth holding onto: the sixth extinction isn’t only a story of loss. It’s also a story of possibility. The very same forces that can cause destruction? We can turn them around. We have the power to protect what’s left, to restore what’s been damaged, and to dream up new ways of living that actually work in harmony with the earth.
Sure, the road ahead isn’t always clear. But it’s not without hope, either. Every action—no matter how small—becomes a thread in the tapestry of life. In the end, the legacy of the sixth extinction won’t just be written in the fossil record. It’ll be shaped by the choices we make, day after day.
